newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB wants St George meeting on merger.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB wants St George meeting on merger.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd has expressed disappointment St George Bank Ltd's friendly takeover offer for Advance Bank Australia Ltd does not need to be be approved by St George shareholders.
But NAB, owner of at least 6.8 percent of St George, declined on Monday to comment on whether it was exploring legal or other options to block the deal.
"We are disappointed there would not be a shareholders meeting and we were concerned about the level of information out there about a merger proposal," NAB spokesman David Upton said.

"Given there hasn't been any details of the merger released as yet, we thought it would be important to have a meeting to give shareholders an opportunity to discuss it and find out more," Upton said.
He declined to comment when asked about a newspaper comment that NAB might have few legal options to oppose the bid.
"We simply wanted to make known that we were disappointed that there wouldn't be a meeting," he said.
St George's scrip and cash offer valued each Advance Bank share at A$7.30 -- or nearly three times net asset backing.

A broker told Reuters that several institutional investors in St George were also lobbying for a shareholders' meeting to discuss the merger, but the institutions said to be involved were not immediately available for comment on Monday.
"Three institutions...are a little bit up in arms about it and would like to see a meeting," the broker told Reuters.

NAB has declined to comment on reports that it added to its St George stake last Thursday, when St George's share price closed 55 cents higher. St George shares were trading at A$8.90 at 0140 GMT (12.40 p.m.), up nine cents on Friday's close.
